author: Autodesk
description: MPM sand scene that shows instancing workflow
documentation:
## MPM Sand Grain Instances

### Description

This graph demonstrates how to activate and simulate sand using the MPM solver. After the simulation, there is a portion of the graph dedicated to creating instance geometry that will be rendered. In this case, cubes are used to represent grains of sand. The main purpose is to provide a surface to catch specular highlights. These highlights will change over the course of the simulation as the grains rotate based on the MPM solve. A `standard_surface_mat` defines the look of the sand and demonstrates how to connect the point_color to the material in the graph.

### Inputs, Controls & Outputs

The Main control for this graph is the quality switch. There are values for the voxel size that changes the detail and count of particles per voxel when the grains are initially sourced. This allows for the quick execution of the graph at a low quality to preview the workflow. Once the workflow is understood and tweaks as desired, it's potentially good time to use the high quality voxel size and dedicate more time to simulate and render a more detailed result. This technique is often helpful when modifying a simulation to work quickly, then run a high quality result after details like timing and/or influences are worked out in rapid iterations.

The output (through a final terminal) are point instances. The instances carry the necessary properties to orient, scale, and color the geometry, as well as provide the velocity to define how motion blur is applied (if enabled in the render settings). While working in Bifrost, the proxy terminal is enabled to quickly view the simulated points without having to fully instance them in the viewport.

### Workflow and Tips

In addition to the quality switch, the `mpm_settings_to_scatter_density` is what determines how many points are scattered in the volume create from source geometry. The `scatter_points` node is limited to 1,000,000 points by default. If you want a very large simulation, ensure this number is increased. Otherwise, you may see a sparse looking simulation  due to the million point limit, even though you may have millions of voxels in the actual simulation.

The `file_cache` compound is not required. However, it is strongly recommended to cache out the MPM particles. Do note for efficiency there is an `erase_component_properties` compound before the `file_cache` compound to reduce the file size as many properties are not required outside of the simulation. It also makes it very easy to iterate on the instancing and render settings without having to worry about losing a simulation result once everything is dialed in. Also, once cached, the rendering could be easily distributed to a render farm if that is available.

_notes.text: Source geometries need to be converted to volumes
Density setting is taken from the MPM settings

The file_cache is set to passthrough.
When running the simulation at production resolution it is ideal to cache out the simulation data before rendering, as typically the render will take longer than the simulation and can be easily resumed (unlike the simulation)
